name: ocr-to-text
h1: OCR API for Bulk Scanned PDFs and Images in One Run
metaTitle: Bulk OCR API: Scanned PDFs & Images to Text | ActorForge
metaDescription: One OCR API for mixed batches of scanned PDFs, PNG, JPEG, TIFF and more. Tesseract 5, 29 languages, per-page confidence. $3 per 1,000 OCR pages.
tagline: A general-purpose OCR endpoint for pipelines that receive a bit of everything: scanned PDFs, phone photos, TIFF faxes and screenshots.
intro: Document intake is rarely tidy. One supplier emails a scanned PDF, another sends a phone photo of the same invoice, the fax gateway produces TIFFs and a support form uploads screenshots. Building a separate path for each format is busywork. The OCR to Text actor takes all of them in one `urls` list and returns text in a consistent row format.

It accepts PDF, PNG, JPEG, TIFF, WebP, GIF, BMP and JPEG 2000. Each image counts as one page; each PDF is read page by page, with pages that already have a text layer read directly at a tenth of the OCR price. By default you get one row per file with all its text, which keeps downstream code simple whatever the input type.

Under the hood it runs Tesseract 5 with LSTM models in 29 languages, up to 4 per run. That makes it a good fit for automation work: back-office pipelines, AI agents that need a reliable OCR tool, and scheduled batch jobs where a run budget cap matters. Failed downloads, unreadable files and blank pages are never charged.
howItWorks: You submit a list of file links in `urls`, mixing PDFs and image formats freely, and optionally cap the batch with `maxFiles`.
The actor detects each file's type; images go straight to OCR, PDFs are split into pages and text-layer pages are read without OCR in `auto` mode.
Tesseract 5 recognises the image pages in your chosen `languages`, dropping low-confidence words if you set `minWordConfidence`.
Each file becomes one dataset row by default (`outputMode` `document`), or one row per PDF page if you switch to `pages`.
Charges are per page read, and the run stops cleanly when it reaches the maximum total charge you set.
outputNote: The sample shows a scanned PDF, a TIFF test image and a digital PDF processed in the same run, each as one row with its file type and page counts.

useCases.title: Back-office document intake
useCases.text: Route every incoming attachment, whatever its format, to one OCR call and store the text next to the file. Because each file comes back as one row with `fileType`, `pagesOcr` and `confidence`, the same parser handles invoices, letters and forms.

useCases.title: OCR tool for AI agents
useCases.text: Give an agent one tool that turns any document link into text instead of separate image and PDF tools. The confidence score lets the agent decide when to ask a human to check a result.

useCases.title: Migrating a document store
useCases.text: When moving years of scans out of an old document management system, export file links in batches of up to 10,000 per run with `maxFiles` and keep the returned text for search in the new system.

useCases.title: Scheduled nightly OCR jobs
useCases.text: Run the actor on a schedule against the day's new uploads and set a maximum total charge. If a batch is unexpectedly large the run stops at the cap rather than overrunning your budget.

comparisonNote: If you only ever process one kind of file, a dedicated tool such as [PDF OCR](actor:pdf-ocr) or [Image to Text OCR](actor:image-to-text-ocr) gives you the same engine with defaults tuned for that input. Teams with strict data residency needs may still prefer a self-hosted OCR service.

faq.q: Can I send PDFs and images to the same OCR API call?
faq.a: Yes. Put any mix of PDF, PNG, JPEG, TIFF, WebP, GIF, BMP and JPEG 2000 links in `urls`. Images are always one row each; PDFs are one row per file by default or one row per page with `outputMode` set to `pages`.

faq.q: Which OCR languages are supported and how many can I use at once?
faq.a: 29 languages, including English, German, French, Spanish, Arabic, Hebrew, Hindi, Russian, Chinese (simplified and traditional), Japanese, Korean and Thai. You can select up to 4 per run. Modern Greek is not available.

faq.q: How many files can one run handle?
faq.a: `maxFiles` defaults to 1,000 and can be raised to 10,000 per run. Individual files can be up to 100 MB, and PDFs up to 2,000 pages each (200 by default via `maxPagesPerPdf`).

faq.q: Am I charged for files that fail?
faq.a: No. Failed downloads, unreadable files, blank pages and links that return a web page instead of a file are reported in the dataset and not charged. You pay $0.003 per OCR'd page and $0.0003 per PDF page read from its text layer.

faq.q: How do I cut noise from stamps and stains?
faq.a: Set `minWordConfidence` to drop words Tesseract is unsure about. The README suggests 40 to 60 removes most noise from stains and stamps; 0 keeps everything.
